title: Same-field lifting over the image of a universally injective stack morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, representability by algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; smoothness is tested on scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Its underlying point space consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$. Say that $f$ is universally injective if for every morphism of algebraic stacks $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$, the map $|\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z|\to|\mathcal Z|$ is injective. Suppose that $f$ is universally injective. For every algebraically closed field $K$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] with $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, and every object $y\in\mathcal Y(K)$ whose underlying point $[y]$ belongs to the image of $|f|:|\mathcal X|\to|\mathcal Y|$, there are an object $x\in\mathcal X(K)$ and an isomorphism $f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y$ in $\mathcal Y(K)$. The field $K$ itself is used for the lift, without replacing it by an extension.

source.place: Tag 0DTM (lemma-universally-injective-point), including its complete statement; universal injectivity is definition-universally-injective in the same section.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal P=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\operatorname{Spec}K$ using [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Its objects are triples $(x,y,\alpha:f(x)\simeq y)$, with the specified pullback of $y$. The image hypothesis and the definition of equality of point classes give a common field extension over which $y$ is isomorphic to an image object, hence a field-valued object of $\mathcal P$; thus $|\mathcal P|$ is nonempty. The map $\mathcal P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is universally injective: each of its base changes is, by associativity of the triple construction, a base change of $f$. A $K$-object of $\mathcal P$ will give exactly the required object and isomorphism.

Apply [lem-sfb-stack-locally-closed-finite-type-point] to the whole nonempty point space of $\mathcal P$. This supplies a field $L$ and a locally finite type representative $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal P$. Its structural map makes $L$ a field extension of $K$. The representative is representable by algebraic spaces by [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability]. No flatness of $a$, reduction of $\mathcal P$, or local Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

Put $R=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\mathcal P}\operatorname{Spec}L$. This is an algebraic space by representability of $a$. Both projections to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ are locally of finite type, being base changes of $a$, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. By [lem-sfb-stack-universal-injectivity-criteria], the relative diagonal $\Delta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P\times_K\mathcal P$ is surjective on points. It is representable: a scheme test of it is the sheaf of isomorphisms between the two tested objects, which is the corresponding scheme base change of the representable diagonal over $S$. Therefore [lem-sfb-representable-stack-point-surjectivity] makes its base change
$$R\longrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L$$
surjective. The identification with this base change sends an isomorphism between two pullbacks of $a$ to the matching pair; it is the triple description of the 2-fibre product.

The affine tensor-product construction identifies $T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B$ for $B=L\otimes_K L$: the two ring maps into $B$ are $l\mapsto l\otimes1$ and $l\mapsto1\otimes l$, and their universal property is [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], dual to the affine spectrum and fibre-product universal properties. The ring $B$ is nonzero: by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](2) with $C=L$ and $f=g=\mathrm{id}_L$, multiplication $l\otimes l'\mapsto ll'$ is a ring map from $B$ to the field $L$. Suppose $B$ had a nonzero zero-divisor. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-type-limit](2), there are finitely generated $K$-subalgebras $R',S'\subseteq L$ such that $R'\otimes_KS'$ has a nonzero zero-divisor. As subrings of the field $L$, both are domains, and $S'$ is a finite type $K$-algebra. Since $K$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-finite-type-tensor-domain] with $R=R'$ and $S=S'$ says that $R'\otimes_KS'$ is a domain, a contradiction. Hence $B$ is a domain. Its zero prime is a point of $T$. Surjectivity in step 3 gives a field-valued point $r:\operatorname{Spec}F\to R$ mapping to this zero prime. Thus $B\to F$ is injective: its kernel is precisely the prime corresponding to the image point. Apply [lem-sfb-space-two-field-scalar-algebraicity] to $R$ with its two locally finite type maps to $\operatorname{Spec}L$. For every $\lambda\in L$ this makes the image of $\lambda\otimes1$ algebraic over the image of $1\otimes L$ in $F$.

Fix $\lambda\in L$. The algebraicity from step 4 gives coefficients $b_0,\ldots,b_n\in L$, not all zero, with $\sum_i b_i\lambda_1^i=0$ in $F$, where $\lambda_1$ is the image of $\lambda\otimes1$ and $b_i$ is embedded from the second factor. The injection $B\hookrightarrow F$ gives $\sum_i\lambda^i\otimes b_i=0$ in $L\otimes_K L$. If $\lambda$ were transcendental over $K$, the finite list $1,\lambda,\ldots,\lambda^n$ would be $K$-linearly independent. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector], extend this list to a $K$-basis of $L$ and take its coordinate functionals $c_j:L\to K$. Applying $c_j\otimes\mathrm{id}_L$ to that relation gives $b_j=0$ for every $j$, a contradiction. Thus every $\lambda\in L$ is algebraic over $K$. This is a finite linear-independence argument in the defining tensor product, not a new geometric assertion.

Since $K$ is algebraically closed, each nonzero polynomial over $K$ factors into linear factors over $K$ by successive extraction of roots. Its value at any element of the field $L$ can vanish only when one linear factor vanishes. The algebraicity just proved therefore implies $L=K$ through its specified structural embedding. Transport $a$ along the inverse of this field isomorphism to obtain a $K$-object of $\mathcal P$. Projecting the triple gives $x\in\mathcal X(K)$ and its specified isomorphism $f(x)\simeq y$. The lift uses $K$ itself.
